scraped.scraped_description: The official home page of the LiquidFeedback project.

name: LiquidFeedback
tagline: Liquid democracy software for transparent proposal development and collective decision-making
org_type: open-source project with commercial service arm
sdg_alignment: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
known_funders: European Commission (Horizon 2020 — WeGovNow and CO3 projects)
awards: SuMa Award 2011 (SuMa e.V. — Association for Free Access to Knowledge)

policy_outcomes.description: Pirate Party Germany Berlin used LiquidFeedback for binding resolutions via a 'Permanent General Assembly' with organ status under party statutes
Friesland County (Germany) used LiquidFeedback for civic participation on county council proposals
Deployed in Athens, London, Paris, Turin, and Venice region as part of EU WeGovNow and CO3 projects

outcome_methodology: case studies and institutional adoption records
published_performance_metrics: User engagement metrics and adoption rates documented in EU WeGovNow and CO3 project reports; case studies on Pirate Party Germany participation rates available in academic literature
documented_limitations: complexity can create barriers for non-technical users
preferential voting and delegation mechanisms require user education
vocal minorities can still dominate unless collective moderation is tuned
failure_modes: low adoption rates within organisations if not mandated
delegation chains can concentrate power in unexpected ways
governance_model: open-source published by Public Software Group e.V.; commercial services by FlexiGuided GmbH; research by Interaktive Demokratie e.V.
curation_criteria: Proposals are curated through community moderation, issue tracking, and delegation mechanisms; contributors must sign contributor licence agreement; governance follows MIT/X11 open-source licence terms
contributor_governance: contributor licence agreement required; MIT/X11 licence
disparity_tracking: No formal disparity tracking documented; accessibility concerns noted regarding digital divide and technical literacy barriers for non-technical users
community_ownership: Open-source governance model with Public Software Group e.V. as steward; community contributions welcome under CLA; commercial services managed separately by FlexiGuided GmbH
controversies: Pirate Party Germany experienced internal debates about the legitimacy and representativeness of LiquidFeedback-driven decisions
political_bias_allegations: No documented allegations of political bias; however, concerns raised about whether liquid democracy mechanisms inherently favor certain political ideologies or organisational structures
legal_regulatory_issues: LiquidFeedback is a registered trademark in the EU and USA

elections_used_in.organisation: Pirate Party Germany (national and state branches)
elections_used_in.use: party conference motions and binding resolutions

ai_involvement: No AI or machine learning components documented; system relies on algorithmic voting and delegation mechanisms but not artificial intelligence
political_relevance_summary: LiquidFeedback addresses the civic problem of lowering barriers to civic participation. It has documented policy impact.

movement_building_utility.notes: Directly supports organizers/campaigners through Liquid democracy software for transparent proposal development and collective decision-making.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase enables replication. already deployed internationally across multiple jurisdictions.
